prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a low-speed head-on collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1188; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition, except those allegations expressly admitted herein, and demands strict proof thereof as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant generally denies each allegation and requests that Plaintiff be required to prove the charges and allegations against Defendant by a preponderance of the evidence.

As affirmative defenses, Defendant asserts the following. First, the collision was a low-speed impact, and Plaintiff's claimed injuries were not caused by the occurrence in question but by preexisting conditions or subsequent events unrelated to it. Second, Plaintiff failed to exercise ordinary care for her own safety, and her own negligence proportionately reduces or bars any recovery under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code. Third, Plaintiff failed to mitigate her alleged damages by timely pursuing reasonable medical care and treatment, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.

Defendant reserves the right to amend this Answer as discovery proceeds.
